title: Fail closed when ModuleRuntime has no policy
goal: Prevent ModuleRuntime from executing modules when no explicit policy evaluator has been injected, while preserving intentional test behavior through explicit test policies.
context: ModuleRuntime currently treats its optional policy as a skip switch: if nil, it validates only grantedCapabilities and executes module code. M3/M4 composition roots and several direct test constructors omit policy. M6/M7 now forward injected policy, and M8 already supplies resolvedPolicy; the remaining legacy paths need explicit wiring and regression coverage.
forbidden_changes: Do not grant permissions implicitly or change DefaultPolicyEvaluator semantics.
Do not change UI, provider, storage, or Xcode project files.
Do not treat approval-required decisions as approved.
acceptance_criteria: A direct ModuleRuntime call with no policy is rejected before module code executes.
M3 and M4 roots expose optional policy injection and pass it to ModuleRuntime; omission remains fail-closed.
Existing tests that intentionally exercise module execution inject an explicit test policy.
Denied policy, capability-grant checks, cancellation, and output validation retain regression coverage.
verification: Check Swift package tests + repository integrity and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA CI.
recovery: If required CI exposes unhandled callers, keep the PR open and migrate those callers in this same logical task; do not merge while policy-free execution remains possible.
